title: Narrative-led component lexicon and provenance kit for Console patterns
creator: Asha Ribeiro
description: Create a coherent, narrative-driven component lexicon and provenance kit that documents origin, intended usage, and constraints for console UI primitives used across dashboards, rollout controls, and cost views. Deliver a Figma library with source-of-truth variants, a lightweight migration guide for engineers, and a provenance sheet that maps components to squads and rollouts.
context: Multiple teams have independently created variants of panels, compact cards, and status rails for cost and rollout surfaces. This has led to inconsistent behavior (spacing, focus states, token use) and duplicated Figma components. Past audits flagged fragmentation during the Dedicated surface redesign and a cross-team post-mortem recommended a stronger single source of truth with clear ownership.
proposal: 1) Define a short, narrative lexicon: semantic names (eg. 'InfoStrip' vs 'MetricTile'), usage notes and do/don't examples for each primitive. 2) Build a provenance kit: a machine-readable CSV and human-friendly sheet that records creation author, owning squad, last reviewed date, and dependent routes/dashboards. 3) Publish a Figma component library with canonical variants and token mappings (color, spacing, elevation). 4) Ship a migration checklist for engineers and PMs with concrete steps: replace old components, deprecate variants, update tests and storybook entries.
acceptance_criteria: Figma library contains canonical components for dashboard cards, rollout rails, cost mini-cards with at least 3 responsive variants each
Provenance sheet (spreadsheet) lists owner, created_at, last_reviewed for every component; no missing owners
Design playbook page published in Confluence with usage examples and do/don't guidance
One cross-functional review session completed with PMs and two engineering squads; notes captured and action items assigned
Migration checklist created and validated by a small pilot replacing 2 dashboard instances
All visual examples meet WCAG AA contrast for normal text and have keyboard focus states documented
notes: Prefer semantic component names that describe purpose rather than visual treatment. Keep spacing scale tied to existing platform baseline (4px) but allow a responsive step for compact surfaces. For provenance, include links to the canonical storybook or runtime route where possible. We will not immediately rename every existing component; aim for a sacrificial deprecation period and automated linting to detect legacy usage.
